Retrieve diagnostics from multiScaleR objects

Source: R/diagnostics.R
diagnostics.Rd

Returns structured warning/diagnostic information stored on fitted multiScaleR objects. Diagnostics are populated automatically during multiScale_optim and flag potential issues with the optimization result.

Usage

diagnostics(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'multiScaleR'
diagnostics(object, ...)

Arguments

object

An object to inspect. Must be of class multiScaleR.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

Value

A named list with the following elements:

max_distance

A list describing whether the estimated scale of effect approaches or exceeds max_D. Fields include: triggered (logical), variables (names of affected covariates), effective_distance (estimated 90% one-dimensional kernel distance per covariate; see kernel_dist), max_D (the limit used), ratio (max_D / effective_distance), and suggested_max_D (a recommended minimum max_D value). Triggered when max_D / effective_distance < 2.

sigma_precision

A list describing whether sigma estimates are imprecise. Fields include: triggered (logical), variables (names of affected covariates), estimate (sigma means), se (standard errors), and se_to_mean (ratio of SE to mean). Triggered when SE / Mean >= 0.5 for any covariate. NULL when no precision concern was flagged.

shape_precision

Identical structure to sigma_precision but for the shape parameter of the exponential power kernel. NULL unless kernel = "expow" was used and a precision concern arose.

sample_size

A list with fitted_n, the number of observations in the final model, and prepared_n, the number of observations in the preparation object, or model rows for repeated-site unmarked data. For unmarked fits, prepared_sites is the number of distinct spatial sites in the preparation object. triggered is TRUE when the fitted model uses fewer observations. Candidate scales that change the initial model's sample are rejected during optimization.

start_stall

For the default refit backend, present only when the optimizer returned its starting values, so the reported scales are those starts. A search from the default start is flagged whenever it returns that start. A user-supplied or screened start is flagged only when the search stopped after one evaluation, because such a start may already be an optimum. Fields include reason, screened (whether the start came from start_strategy = "screen"), start (starting sigma values in map units), function_evaluations, and message, which names the remedy. reason is "hard_radius" when every optimized scale is a hard radius, as under kernel = "fixed". Its likelihood changes in steps, so the gradient is zero almost everywhere. reason is "refit_failed" when no refitted model gave a finite log-likelihood at the start. A glmmTMB model with a non-positive-definite Hessian reports none. reason is "no_progress" otherwise. A warning gives the same message when the fit is made, and print() and summary() repeat it.

refit_hessian

For the default refit backend, retains the outer curvature status and active smooth-parameter mask. A bound table records estimates, lower/upper bounds in reporting units, and bound flags. If any active parameter is within 1e-5 log units of a positive bound, joint outer Wald SEs are withheld. A zero lower bound is flagged only when reached. The original curvature status is retained separately. A status of "hessian_includes_failed_refit" means a refit failed at one of the finite-difference points used for the Hessian, so its curvature reflects the failure penalty; Wald SEs are withheld and a warning is given. This is a numerical support flag, not a test of identification or a calibrated confidence limit. Native coefficient covariance and parameter counts are unchanged.

radius_profile

For a declared radius grid, one row per combination. radius, or one radius:<predictor> column per hard radius, uses map units. Any sigma:<predictor> and shape:<predictor> columns hold the reoptimized smooth bandwidths in map units and unitless shapes, respectively. The table also reports native log_likelihood, status (scored or failed), any failure message, and a logical selected flag. With smooth predictors, smooth_starts holds a table of optimizer and convergence diagnostics for each combination that reached the smooth search. An all-failed search carries the profile table on the error condition.

profile_glm

Present for both opt-in analytic GLM backends. Includes uncertainty_available, explanatory reasons, weak_identifiability, boundary, condition_number, log-kernel standard errors, competing-mode flags, and attempted/eligible start counts. poisson_limit marks negligible fitted NB2 extra variance; poisson_compatible and poisson_deviance compare the NB2 fit with a Poisson fit at the selected kernel scales. See multiScale_optim for thresholds and limitations.

Details

These diagnostics are evaluated automatically at the end of multiScale_optim. Console warnings are printed when any diagnostic is triggered and verbose = TRUE. diagnostics() provides programmatic access to the same information without re-running the model. These stored diagnostics retain the historical 1D 90% distance and threshold, independently of the new 2D reporting default in plots and summaries. Changing dimension when reporting a fit does not recompute its stored diagnostics. Use kernel_dist(object) to inspect the ideal planar radius separately.

When max_distance is triggered, consider re-running kernel_prep with a larger max_D value. The suggested minimum is stored in suggested_max_D.

When sigma_precision is triggered, the variable may not have a meaningful scale of effect, or the data may be insufficient to estimate it precisely. Interpret affected covariates with caution.

See also

multiScale_optim, kernel_prep

Examples

# \donttest{
data('pts')
data('count_data')
hab <- terra::rast(system.file('extdata', 'hab.tif', package = 'multiScaleR'))

kernel_inputs <- kernel_prep(pts = pts,
                             raster_stack = hab,
                             max_D = 250,
                             kernel = 'gaussian')
#> 
#> No sigma values provided...
#> Creating necessary elements to optimize sigma
#> 
#> Extracting values from raster layers...

mod <- glm(y ~ hab, family = poisson, data = count_data)
opt <- multiScale_optim(fitted_mod = mod, kernel_inputs = kernel_inputs)
#> 
#> 
#> Optimization complete
#> 
#>  WARNING!!!
#>  The estimated scale of effect approaches or exceeds the current search extent.
#>  Consider increasing max_D in `kernel_prep` to >=250.56 to ensure accurate estimation of scale.
#> 
#> 

## Access diagnostics
diag <- diagnostics(opt)
diag$max_distance$triggered
#> [1] TRUE
diag$sigma_precision
#> NULL
# }
